Single-work metadata was retrievable, so publication status is verified but citing work is not. This is the one gap that could overturn the surviving candidate.

The surviving candidate C1 was narrowed after a second full-text pass: LIBERO-RIG already defines 'tolerance per axis' (Table 5) and More Structure already demonstrates the mechanism (spatial grounding fixes Near-Miss 31%->2.5% but leaves No-Grasp unchanged). What remains untested is only the cross-task predictive relation, and no pilot evidence exists that same-task/different-failure-mode variants can be constructed.
41 of 92 registered papers were read at abstract level only (arXiv HTML rate limits); they may contain direct competitors that would change the crowding judgement.
Conference-versus-arXiv version differences were not compared for most entries.
Real-robot evidence in this literature rests on 20-30 trials per condition, which limits the statistical strength of any action-level claim, including future ones.
Whether a measurement/prediction contribution is acceptable as the master's small paper is an advisor judgement that literature research cannot settle.
conclusion: After 130 queries and 92 registered papers, and after a second full-text pass that corrected an over-optimistic first assessment, five of seven directions fail the hard vetoes (cross-view consistency, 3D representation upgrades, active re-observation, spatial-interface design, phase-localised grounding diagnosis). One direction survives only in a narrowed, medium-low-confidence form: whether the composition of baseline failures (spatial-precision vs tracking/occlusion) plus the intervention's reduction of the operative spatial error predicts the action benefit of a spatial upgrade across held-out tasks. Its mechanism is already demonstrated on a single task and per-axis tolerance is already operationalised, so the remaining contribution is a cross-task prediction study whose feasibility is unverified. The report recommends no experiment until six explicit gates are met, and states that if the predictive relation does not hold, no candidate in this scope qualifies.
